- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and price drops >2%, model frequently fails to adjust; apply downward bias of 1–2% per negative sentiment day.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often overfits recent volatility; use 14-day EWMA instead of 30-day forecast for smoother correction.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast for 3 consecutive days, apply “lag correction”: subtract 0.5–1.0% from next forecast to account for delayed reaction.
